The code is good. One item is requested before merge: screenshots.

What I checked in the code:

- `controller.post` reads through `parse_post_name` (shape only: a non-empty string, trimmed); a bad value is refused at the key's name. The registry rule (a built-in name that serves the kind) is `post_name_refusal`, and the registry reaches the post crate through a closure, as the holder lookup does (#828). No new crate edge; the decision record is in `docs/decisions/2374-machine-names-its-post.md`.
- `post_offer_for`: the machine's named post wins over the kind offer; it is offered only when it is in the registry, serves the mount, and differs from the setup's post. `PostRef::Builtin` and a named `Fanuc` compare by name, so the default document is never offered its own post. A `File` post is never second-guessed, as before.
- The Setup banner shows the reason ("the machine names X as its post; switch to it?" / the old kind wording); the Machines editor draws a dropdown with `(none)` for "not stated", and `post_choices` lists only the posts that serve the machine's kind. The `Switch post` button takes the existing `SelectPostNamed` command, so undo works as the law asks.
- MCP: `get_job` and `load_machine` answer through one `offer_view`, so a person and an agent are told the same thing. The `post` tool now lists every built-in post. The shipped grblHAL, TinyG, Haas, Tormach, Makera, Sienci and Doosan mill files name their post, and `machine_library` checks each shipped file.
- Provenance: one line, names the public sources. Clean-room: original key and rule, from the issue.

Local results (built and tested on this head, LinuxCNC worktree):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 12 binaries, all passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test machine_library --test mcp_machine_post --test plasma_post`: 14 + 4 + 5 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1046 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Requested before merge:

1. PR body, `Screenshots`: add viewable before and after images. This PR changes what a user sees: the Machines editor's post field becomes a dropdown, and the Setup banner gets the new "the machine names ..." line. The project asks each UI PR for both images in the body. Post them as release assets or upload them into the PR, and link them from the body.

No other blockers. The PR is ready; I leave it as its author set it. A maintainer approves and merges by hand.

Screenshots added to the PR body: the Setup banner and the Machines editor's Post row, before and after, plus the dropdown open. Images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. No code change; the head is still `b6bc94239`.
This PR goes to draft for a push: the maintainer's clear-out order. The push merges main and adds two repairs. A comment with the details follows.

The maintainer ordered a clear-out of each PR that has `conflicts` or `needs-rework` (2026-11-20). For this PR, our session merged `main`, repaired what `main` changed, gated the result and pushed. The new head is `92c12213f`. Nothing was force-pushed: your commits up to `b6bc94239` are unchanged.

**What changed in this push**

- `6d4e8e6ca`, `f0039291a`: two merges of `origin/main`. There were no conflicts.
- `d33c00f67`: `assets/machines/linuxcnc-3axis.mch` (new on main, #2303) states `"post": "LinuxCNC"`. `MACHINES` pairs the two, so the file follows your pairing rule.
- `fe9e4a4ab`: `assets/machines/grbl-3axis.mch` (new on main, #2481) states `"post": "Grbl 1.1"` for the same reason. Pin for both machines: `machine_library::the_linuxcnc_machine_is_offered_the_linuxcnc_post`.
- `92c12213f`: the example `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` stores its machine. The microARC 4 file now names its post, so the stored machine was stale, and `continuous_4axis_part` was red. The test's own update path (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`) saved the project again. The only change is `"post": "Tormach PathPilot"` under `/machine/machine`.

**Proof that the posted program does not change**

- The update path also writes the `.nc`. We did not take that `.nc`. On this branch, it changes 7 `A` words by one last digit.
- The same command on plain main `08697d3c4` changes the same 7 lines in the same way. The two regenerated programs are byte-identical. Thus the drift is on main, not in this PR. We filed #3063 (P7) for it.
- The tests that load the old committed projects (no `post` key) and compare the posted program byte for byte are green: `first_4axis_part`, `first_router_part` and `tilt_basis_compat`.

**Gate**

- A stacked batch run on Windows (main `ee91ac3e5` and nine PRs) had 998 steps. The targets of this PR were green. One step was red: `continuous_4axis_part`. This push repairs it.
- Our runs on the head `92c12213f`, debug, `-j 18`:
  - `camcraft-app`: `continuous_4axis_part` 10, `first_4axis_part` 4, `first_router_part` 4, `machine_library` 15, `mcp_machine_post` 4, `plasma_post` 5, `tilt_basis_compat` 7. All passed.
  - `camcraft-post` lib: 83 passed.
  - `camcraft-ui` lib, `machine_named_post` and `machines_edit`: 9 passed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**Open follow-up (recommended P7, not a blocker)**

`LoadMachine::from_file` and `LoadMachine::builtin` only parse a file. They do not validate it. A machine file that names an unknown post mounts, and the Setup page then shows no offer and no message. The setup's post does not change, so the output stays correct. The Machines pane and `from_catalogue` refuse the name. We recommend that the banner and the MCP `post_offer` name the unknown post.

The screenshots in the PR body are still valid. This push does not change the UI.

Thank you for the work, `roer70`. Nothing was force-pushed.

Ready for a re-check.

- A machine file names its post at `controller.post`. The Machines editor shows a Post row with a dropdown of the built-in posts that serve the machine's kind. - The machine-library change keeps `posts: Vec<&'static str>` as the built-in list; the per-file name is separate. 35 `.mch` files gained the key; the shipped Tormach, Grbl, Heidenhain and LinuxCNC kinds read right.
- MCP is kept in step: `load_machine` and `get_job` report the post the machine names (2d26ef2a3). The decision file `docs/decisions/2374-machine-names-its-post.md` is in the PR. New UI test `machine_named_post.rs` (85 lines) plus updated `machines_edit.rs` pins. All touched files stay under 400 lines.
- The screenshot item is met: the body carries five before/after images pinned to commit c15c4c720 (the Setup banner pair, the editor General pair, and the open dropdown). I checked all five: each answers 200 and shows the named item.
